newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Matra to flesh out Hungary offset deal.
newsitem.headline: Matra to flesh out Hungary offset deal.

text.p: Details of the offset plan included in France's Matra Defense's $100 million air defence missile deal with Hungary are still to be fleshed out, Hungary's industry and trade ministry said on Thursday.
The contract, the first ever formal offset deal signed by Hungary for a military procurement contract, was announced by the defence ministry on Wednesday.

"The French company undertakes to provide offset for the contract and there are also the necessary legal and financial guarantees to make sure these offset undertakings are realised," Peter Balas, the ministry official in charge of offset deals, told Reuters.

"How this offset will be realised is for the future. The agreement only sets the general framework conditions but it is up to Matra to make sure that these offset undertakings are fulfilled -- there are no specific companies or products chosen as yet".
Balas confirmed that the whole of the deal is subject to offset arrangements, which involve both investment in and purchases from Hungary's manufacturing sector.
Colonel Jeno Kopasz, head of of the defence ministry's procurement office told Reuters on Wednesday deliveries of the missiles would start this year and be completed by the end of the century.
Matra will provide training for Hungarian troops both in Hungary and in France, Kopasz said.
Hungary, which started the modernisation of its army woth a view to NATO membership, announced the first tender for the anti-aircraft missiles last September.
The other bidders were Daimler-Benz, Sweden's Bofors, Bombardier unit Short Brothers of Northern Ireland and Hughes Electronics of the U.S.

Hungary is expected to prepare an international tender for upgrading its radar system -- a deal of similar magnitude to the missile purchase -- as well as a $700 million to $800 million tender for some 30 fighter jets soon after its status with NATO becomes clear at the alliance's Madrid summit.
Hungary, the Czech Republic and Poland are expected to be invited to join NATO during the meeting.

A number of offset programmes connected with the fighter tender, notably with Saab of Sweden and Lockheed Martin LK.N and McDonnell Douglas of the U.S. have been set up but these are not linked directly with the actual procurement, Balas said.

"These were pre-contract activities the companies undertook to increase their purchase and investment," he said. "This offset performance is recorded but it is not actually put to use as long as there is no tender for the fighters and until there is a winner."
